query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Addition of 2 at.% Cu into MnNiSi Heusler‐type alloy will improve fracture toughness by at least 20% while retaining at least 90% of the peak magnetocaloric entropy change (ΔS_max) compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline MnNiSi Heusler‐type alloy (stoichiometric composition MnNiSi) in as-cast condition.
generation.intervention: Substitutional doping of 2 at.% Cu on the Ni sublattice during alloy melt and casting.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure; magnetocaloric and mechanical tests performed at temperatures in the martensitic‐to‐austenitic transition range (280–320 K); magnetic field change of 2 T for ΔS measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of fine Cu‐rich precipitates at and near grain boundaries leading to grain refinement and impediment of crack propagation.
generation.mechanism: Cu segregation at grain boundaries strengthens intergranular cohesion, reduces brittleness, and increases toughness without significantly disrupting the Mn–Ni–Si magnetic exchange interactions responsible for the large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fracture toughness (K_IC) increases by ≥20%, while the peak magnetic entropy change ΔS_max decreases by no more than 10% relative to the undoped baseline.
generation.baseline: Undoped MnNiSi alloy prepared and tested under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: Cu doping within ±0.5 at.% of the 2 at.% target; temperature tests strictly within 280–320 K; magnetic field changes of 2 T.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in the exact retention of ΔS_max since Cu effects on magnetic ordering in MnNiSi are not yet quantitatively established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloy batches (undoped MnNiSi and MnNiSi + 2 at.% Cu) via identical arc‐melting and annealing schedules. Measure fracture toughness using single‐edge notched‐bend (SENB) tests and quantify ΔS_max by magnetometry under a 2 T field around the martensitic transition.
measurements: Peak magnetic entropy change ΔS_max under ΔH=2 T
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the Cu‐doped sample shows K_IC <1.2× K_IC(baseline) or ΔS_max <0.9× ΔS_max(baseline).
